A1.justification: Both PDFs describe JudgeBench and contain readable main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Corresponding material can be matched reliably despite additions, renumbering, and page reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of judges and reward models, benchmark comparisons, solver-versus-judge experiments, and response-generator and fine-tuned-judge analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds reasoning-model evaluations, an augmented knowledge-subset experiment, and response-length measurements.

M1.justification: The single-model response-generation pipeline, correct/incorrect pair selection, correctness filtering, and two-order judgment aggregation remain unchanged. Section 3 rewrites explain the existing procedure without introducing a new component.

E1.justification: Both versions use MMLU-Pro, LiveBench, and LiveCodeBench for the same four task domains and retain the prior-benchmark comparisons. Enlarging the knowledge subset changes sample count, without establishing new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds o3-mini at three reasoning levels and DeepSeek-R1 to the Arena-Hard comparison. All eleven previously evaluated models remain, and comparator membership in the other existing experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluations compare low, medium, and high o3-mini reasoning settings. Appendix A.3 additionally evaluates six judges on 770 knowledge pairs versus the original 154. These supplement the unchanged 350-pair main evaluation and judgment-aggregation protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a sample-size sensitivity check, and new Appendix A.4 compares correct and incorrect response lengths to investigate length bias. Table 2 also provides reasoning-effort sensitivity results. Existing ablations and fine-tuned-judge diagnostics are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, seeds, or repeated-run uncertainty estimates. The two response-order trials are unchanged. Newly reported average response lengths are descriptive results, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing result entries are retained. Table 2 adds o3-mini accuracies of 80.86%, 76.57%, and 70.57%, plus DeepSeek-R1 at 73.14%; o3-mini high becomes the leader while o1-preview remains at 75.43%. Table 8 adds six augmented-subset scores with unchanged rankings, and Appendix A.4 reports mean lengths of 562.29 versus 561.16 tokens.

T1.justification: The conceptual evaluation hierarchy and illustrative mathematical examples are retained. No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about the hierarchical framework, dataset-construction pipeline, and challenging correctness-focused benchmark. Additional evaluations support these contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets stable rankings on the augmented knowledge subset as evidence supporting dataset-size sufficiency. It also newly argues that similar average response lengths demonstrate mitigation of length bias. These interpretations were absent from v1.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4 newly identifies the GPT-4o tokenizer used for response-length measurements. Existing judge implementation details, complete prompt templates, and code/data access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hu et al. (2024) and Wei et al. (2024) to support the length-bias discussion, and contextualizes benchmark size using previously cited datasets. The main related-work discussion and research positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Several introduction and pipeline paragraphs are tightened or rewritten. A new appendix subsection shifts the former A.4 and A.5 to A.5 and A.6, and publication headers are updated. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains four rows and updates its best-score highlighting; Table 8 is newly added. The four existing figures retain their graphics, with a softened Figure 1 caption. Tables and appendix prompt boxes reflow without a broader visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 broadens model comparisons and adds a useful dataset-size stability check in Table 8, modestly strengthening the benchmark's empirical support. Clearer exposition also helps. The length-bias conclusion overstates what nearly equal aggregate mean lengths establish, but the added validation still supports a limited net improvement.
